# Overview

Getting Started

Aircall supports two ways to authenticate with the REST API: Basic Authentication and OAuth.

Use Basic Authentication when you are connecting your own internal tools or private integration to Aircall. Use OAuth when your app needs to access Aircall data on behalf of other users or customers.

Use case  | Basic Authentication  | OAuth
--- | --- | ---
Connect your own system and tools to Aircall  | ✅  | ❌
Build an integration for multiple Aircall users outside
your organization  | ❌  | ✅

This guide explains the two methods in more detail and helps you choose the right authentication method before you start building.

Basic Authentication

Basic Authentication lets you authenticate requests with an `API ID` and `token` that you generate from your Aircall Dashboard.

To connect a tool or service, copy these credentials and paste them into the platform that you want to integrate with. This method does not require an authorization flow. Use Basic Authentication when you want to connect quickly without setting up OAuth.

#### 

When to use Basic Authentication

  * You're connecting your own system or tool to Aircall
  * You don't need to access data on behalf of other users
  * You're building a private integration and are not an approved tech partner

For full technical details, see the REST API reference > Basic Auth

OAuth

OAuth lets your application access Aircall data on behalf of a user after they grant permission. It's more complex to implement than Basic Authentication, but it's the standard approach for integrations that serve multiple customers.

#### 

When to use OAuth

  * You're building an integration for multiple Aircall users
  * Users need to authorize access to their own Aircall accounts
  * You’re building a public integration and are an approved tech partner

For full technical details, see the REST API reference > OAuth

### What’s Next

Choose one of the guides below to continue setting up authentication

  * Authenticate with API Keys
  * Set Up OAuth for Your Integration

MCP FAQs

# MCP FAQs

## 

Frequently asked questions for MCP and Agentic integrations

Do I need to write integration logic for each Aircall feature?

No. You expose tools and resources; Aircall AI decides how and when to sequence them at runtime. You're not hardcoding workflows against our product. The customer specifies some rules when configuring the AI agent.

Can I register more than one MCP?

Yes but if possible we want to keep one MCP per product. Submit your request through the tech partner application explaining why you need multiple.

What if evaluation fails more than once?

We'll keep working through specific feedback with your team round by round. There's no limit on attempts — the goal is a reliable connection, not a fast rejection.

Who do I contact with questions during review?

Use the contact details provided when you sign up as a tech partner — our ecosystem team handles review and evaluation communication directly.

Can I connect to a private MCP

Yes you can connect to a proivate MCP and it will be visible only in your account. However, this is in early stages and takes internal work to get set. Because of that we are evaluating those request on a case by case basis.Contact your Aircall contact for more information.

Does Aircall offer an MCP server

As of this writting we don't offer an MCP servier but stay tuned. We might have news soon.

## Authentication

### Introduction

With Aircall Public API, Authentication can be done through OAuth or Basic Auth.

If you want to build an App for companies using Aircall - this is mainly the case for Technology Partners - please use the OAuth flow. It is a requirement to be listed on the Aircall App Marketplace. You can create a partner-specific account by signing up here!

If you are an Aircall customer, building for your own Aircall account only, the Basic Auth flow will do the trick.

All endpoints behave similarly between the two authentication methods, unless indicated otherwise in the documentation.

# Getting your Aircall API key

The Aircall API allows you to connect your Aircall account with other applications such as CRMs, databases, or internal tools. You can use it to retrieve call data, automate user provisioning, or manage your Aircall contacts through custom scripts.

To access the API securely, Aircall uses API Keys for authentication. Some third-party integrations may also require you to provide an Aircall API key.

## Generate an API key from the Aircall Dashboard

### Steps:

  1. Go to to Aircall Dashboard > Integrations > API keys
Image: Screenshot 2026-07-30 at 14.29.45.png

  3. Click Generate an API key, the green button on the top-right corner(a popup window will appear).
  4. Enter a key name and copy the API ID and API Key.
Image: Screenshot 2025-12-22 at 13.33.53.png

  5. Make sure to save both values in a secure place.
  6. Click Confirm to finalize.

> Important: Keep your API key confidential. Anyone with access to this key can make requests to your Aircall account on your behalf.

You can find further information on how you can start using our Public API to your advantage.

# Using Aircall MCP with AI assistants (beta)

Aircall MCP gives an AI assistant, like Claude or ChatGPT, read-only access to your company's calls and conversation intelligence data. Once connected, you can ask your assistant to search calls, pull transcripts and summaries, or check sentiment and action items, without writing any integration code.

This article explains what Aircall MCP does, what it doesn't do, and how to connect it to Claude Desktop, Claude Code, or ChatGPT/Codex.

> Important: Aircall MCP is currently in beta. To join the beta, contact your Account Manager.

## What is MCP?

MCP (Model Context Protocol) is an open standard for connecting AI assistants to external systems. Where an API is written for developers to call, MCP is written for the assistant itself: it can discover what's available and use it without anyone writing integration code.

### How it works

  1. You connect Aircall to your AI client once, via OAuth, the same way you'd connect any other app.
  2. Aircall's MCP server publishes a catalog of tools it can use, such as "search calls," "get transcripts," and "get sentiment," each with a defined input and output.

## Steps

  1. Basic Authentication description
  2. Get your API ID and API Token credentials
  3. Create a Base64 encoded string with your API credentials
  4. Use this encoded string in your HTTP requests

## 1 - Basic Authentication description

Every request to Aircall Public API must be authenticated and authorized. Aircall implemented Basic Authentication, a simple and secure way to authenticate requests.

Basic Authentication is a simple authentication standard, implemented in the HTTP protocol. Lots of API communications are using it as it is one of the most easy-to-implement authentication method out there and yet really secure, both for the API provider and the API user.

We will see in this tutorial how to send your first authenticated request to Aircall Public API.

## 2 - Get your API ID and API Token credentials

Lots of authentication methods require both a username and a password. Basic Authentication follows this standard as well.

Those username and password credentials are called `api_id` and `api_token` in the Aircall Dashboard.

You can create some in your Company's Settings page. In the API Keys section, click on Add a new API key. Aircall will generate two strings, representing the Basic Authentication `username` and `password`.

Image: Aircall Basic auth

Once generated and before closing the modal, copy and paste those credentials somewhere safe on your comcomputer! The `api_token` (= the `password`) will be presented to you only on API Key creation!
